Former HFSC Chair Patrick McHenry says crypto must lock in its political power now: Congress could be the backstop against a return to the Gensler era

"You have sound law and sound regulation, which creates the perimeter. Then we have to have a sufficient market established and a lot of participants."

"Let's go forward 2 years. And let's say you have another election, and we don't get an explicitly pro crypto president. And they take out all these regulators, and they wanna push regulation the opposite direction."

"To go back to a Gensler era of warfare against crypto. The restriction's gonna be on whether or not we have pro crypto members of the House and the Senate to push back on this."

"This incoming Congress is more pro crypto than the Congress from 6 years ago and 8 years ago. Both parties."

"So we have to lock in the political power that we have and make sure that we remain popular for these politicians to not go after us. That's our strength."

"It is a hugely powerful statement of how far we've come, that politicians have now had to accept. Because they see their constituents like what we're doing in the world of crypto."

Former HFSC Chair Patrick McHenry on the correlation between high inflation and government sentiment

“The key driver there, though, is stepping back over the last 50 years. Wherever you have high inflation in the world, the people hate their government.”

“We have this massive new technology. And it could be great. But here in the short run, though, your job is gone. And that’s just the cost we’re gonna have to pay.”

“That is a complete loser where you take people that have seen their wages not go up, compared to the cost of things they’re buying. They see high gas prices. There’s a war going on. They see chaos in Washington.”

“They see people getting rich in Washington and a more beautiful Washington. And they think, you know what I wanna do? I wanna get rid of those people. I don’t care what the other side of the equation is.”

“I’m not listening to debates here. I see inaction, and I don’t like it. So I’m gonna throw the bums out.”

“It’s not been cast that way. It’s been a cost of living, concern about the war. But it’s a throw the bums out election, and that was vigorously done.”

tweets.text:
Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan on why institutions are only now coming around to $BTC

"Old fact from early days of Bitwise, we've been doing this since 2017, is that our average client allocates to us after 8 meetings."

"If you count from when the ETFs launched, which was like two and a half-ish years ago, if you did a meeting every quarter after they launched, you're just sort of now getting to the point that you're accepting of Bitcoin."

"That number of meetings is what it takes to normalize Bitcoin. There are other great firms doing it. Fidelity and BlackRock and VanEck and Franklin."

"No one just sees it for the first time and accepts it. They see it and they study it. Central banks probably do one meeting a year, but after 8 years, they're going to get there too."

"This sort of rule of eight is sort of how these institutions get onboarded into crypto. I think it's as simple as just the passage of time."

"If it's a $90 trillion market, Bitcoin needs to take a quarter of that market to be worth $1.6 million. It's currently at 5% of that market."

"It's basically a similar risk, mostly a migration risk, not a meltdown risk. That gives me a great deal of confidence for everything except for the corner that you mentioned, which are sort of the Satoshi and pre-2015 coins for Bitcoin."

"I don't think broadly quantum is a risk for crypto because again, that's a migration concern. But the pre-2015 coins is a unique challenge for Bitcoin."

"It is widely discussed. So maybe it is to some degree priced in. I'm still optimistic that the community will arrive at a solution that works for people."

"If somebody asked me what keeps me up at night, that's one of the things that keeps me up at night. It doesn't fundamentally change my thesis for Bitcoin."

The scale of Big Tech's AI future financial obligations is extraordinary:

Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Anthropic, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, Oracle, $ORCL, and Nvidia, $NVDA, have disclosed a combined $4.49 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations.

These include future lease payments that have not yet commenced, data-center commitments, equipment purchases, and other contractual obligations.

Alphabet accounts for the largest amount, at $1.08 trillion, followed by Anthropic, at $865 billion, and Meta, at $810 billion.

By comparison, their combined on-balance-sheet obligations total just $758 billion, consisting of long-term debt and existing lease liabilities.

This means off-balance-sheet commitments are nearly 6 times larger than their on-balance-sheet obligations.

In total, these 7 tech companies face ~$5.25 trillion in combined financial obligations.

The AI infrastructure race is facing enormous future financial commitments.

I’ve been tied up with family issues for the last week (always happens at the worst time), so have only really been able to sit down and look at things properly today.

A few thoughts:

BTC has put in five red weeklies in a row, closed below the 50W MA, and is well within the previous range with the bottom of said range being 60k. It's been hammered with endless bad news and headlines. 

Doesn't feel great, obviously. 

In 2023 when we exited the bear market we saw a sharp drop to the 200DMA and that was bought up and we continued our ascent. We were very close to that level this morning but didn’t quite tag (maybe front run). It sits at $73.2k right now. This was a test I have been expecting as an inevitability since we had our impulse candle.

Buying the 200DMA post bear market exit (if this is that moment) is some of the best execution you could have had and a plan that could be blindly followed without letting outside bias prejudice you.

As an analyst, I can see the other side of the coin: in the context of that previous exiting of bear market moment in 2023 we didn’t have so much sustained weakness, and were above the previous point of breakdown, whereas this time we are below the May highs which is where we broke down from this year.

Not getting the push higher to the 90s has meant we have corrected back into the range, and made this look far more like a deviation rather than a strong exiting of the bear market moment.

Will the bulls step in here at/close to the 200DMA? tbc, there are juicy targets below which seem like they have a realistic shot of hitting now that you finally have indexes likely heading for multi week/multi month correction.

It is a do or die level, as nothing good happens when you accept below the 200DMA. You want to see strength and interested buyers here right now. 

The next best thing if that level fails would be a weekly close no lower than 66k to set a nice macro higher low, would also look like an inverse head and shoulders, which is a good bottoming pattern. Monthly is still bullish and painting this picture. I would very much prefer to not go lower than that. 

I still think the macro bottom is in for Bitcoin, but whenever you accept and linger in a previous range you open up the possibility of the range low hitting (60k) and if that hits, alongside mass panic, does it hold? 

To create new lows you would need a lot of forced selling to happen. Think this could only occur if Saylor gets into trouble, or something similar (always possible ofc). 

We had the set up for Bitcoin to show strength, but ultimately we have fallen back into the range on a sustained basis. This needs to reverse asap for a chance of fucking over the bears. Can't be any delays here.

Good alts will bottom first, as they have been doing. We have so few of them, so it's fairly easy to keep a small watchlist. You can simply ignore everything else. It is a total waste of time and energy and it's all legacy garbage, vapour and failed ideas. Retail and institutions are not coming to buy any of that. 

Either we bottom here, and everything looks pretty damn good in ~6 months.

Or we bottom lower, and everything looks pretty damn good in ~12 months.

I find very few assets attractive when looking forward 5 years from now due to the uncertainty that exists with AI and how long the secular bull has been going. I get the anxiety around AI/quantum for BTC (hence why I also like ZEC), but once it overcomes that it remains one of the few assets that reprices vs everything else given enough time due to sovereign fiscal irresponsibility (not something I see changing). I still see it as a cornerstone asset in a non degen portfolio for the world we currently inhabit.

We are more than a year past the top, so don’t get cute and don't overcomplicate it. Build your exposure and let time do the rest.

tweets.text:
all the studies EAs like to cite about mosquito nets are either done in controlled, non real world conditions, or paid for by EA orgs. 

yes there is evidence net use lowers incidence across certain country-level campaigns but has mass net purchasing lowered malaria incidence in the last decade? no! malaria incidence is up 8.5% in the last decade. if the nets were the cheap panacea the EAs pretend they are, it would be substantially down. the truth is, target populations are saturated with nets, you just can't force them to use them. (nor can you realistically use nets all of the time). 

as you say, the only real solution is environmental interventions like drainage, spraying campaigns, AC, screen windows, which is how malaria disappeared from developed countries.

EAs fixate on the nets because it's a very direct "dollars in utils out" relationship but of course it's not that simple, nothing in international development ever is. the truth is you can't really inject money into a dysfunctional third world state and improve public health outcomes outside of extremely narrow interventions like vaccines, especially not something behavioral and multifaceted like malaria.

THE DAILY METALS PULSE
#Uranium #Copper #Silver #Gold
🌙 Closing Edition | November 9, 2026

METALS REBOUND. TOMORROW BRINGS THE INFLATION TEST.
A softer dollar and retreating oil gave metals breathing room today. But the strongest signals came from the physical market.

☢️ URANIUM — Watch the pounds.
Cameco’s October long-term benchmark stands at $98/lb, versus $91.55 spot. Contract pricing continues to command a premium.

$URG’s Q3 results are scheduled for tonight, with management’s call tomorrow. My focus: production progress, costs and how quickly the US supply rebuild can deliver meaningful volumes.

⚡ COPPER — Scarcity is showing up in premiums.
China’s Yangshan import premium hit a record $230/tonne. Shanghai exchange inventories fell more than 24% last week to just 33,848 tonnes.

Today, Codelco’s chairman warned production would keep falling without private partners developing new projects. A reminder of how difficult replacing supply has become.

🥈 SILVER — Another positive session.
Front-month COMEX futures settled at $52.564, up 1.47%, their highest settlement since October 28. The rebound is building, with tomorrow’s inflation report the next test.

🥇 GOLD — Back above $4,100.
December futures settled at $4,114.50, up 1%. Softer oil eased inflation concerns, while a weaker dollar supported buying.

China also added approximately 25.8 tonnes to its official gold reserves in October—the largest monthly addition in three years.

👀 NEXT: US CPI tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. ET.
A cooler reading could support the rebound. A hotter print could revive pressure from the dollar and interest-rate expectations.

My take: CPI can move metals in minutes. Bringing new mines into production takes years.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily pulse.

Over the weekend I’ve been digging deeper into Mezzanine and am growing increasingly more bullish. I’ve deposited 10k+ of my own funds into the protocol and it’s earning an excellent yield + generating points which I suspect will become quite valuable too in due time.

A bunch of reasons why I am bullish:

 1) The founder, @phtevenstrong, is a true OG in the defi space and has been around for years. He knows how to find the best yields and put together innovative strategies and find edges in places others don’t think to look. He has a great reputation and a lot of connections in the space.

 2) This isn’t some app that has been vibe-coded over a weekend, the first public post was made back in February (https://t.co/beNSZ3Wl20), and they’ve been building in public all year.

 3) The tranches mechanism of allowing users to choose their own risk profile is genuinely interesting, and when coupled with tapping into RWAs for yield generation creates an opportunity not found anywhere else on the market.

 4) It’s early with only ~$5m TVL and one vault so your points per capital deployed ratio is going to be very high. I suspect the TVL is going to grow rapidly as more people discover the platform and more vaults are deployed. I believe they’re aiming for 2-3 per month.

 5) It has some people I really respect as seed investors, like @rektdiomedes who said it’s the first seed investment he’s made in three years (https://t.co/eUkEdprKTn)

 6) They can explain where the yield is coming from and are hyper transparent about everything, see this post to understand how they’re generating yield for their first vault, The Hastra Optimizer (https://t.co/XrjcSSkK8l) 

Yes I partnered with them to help spread the word and will receive some compensation for the whole deal, but I have partnered with many projects over the years and there aren’t that many that I am going and putting 5 figures of my own funds into (more than I’m receiving for our partnership) purely because I think it’s a great protocol and opportunity. With Mezzanine I think it’s a great opportunity.

It’s not without risks ofc, like anything in defi, so please dyor too and only put in funds that you’re comfortable with and that are appropriate for your portfolio and risk profile. 

But I really do recommend checking them out and at least keeping them on your radar. I suspect we’ll be hearing a lot more about Mezzanine in the coming months. This is another post I found which I think offers a really balanced and good perspective, and is also worth reading for those wanting to learn more: https://t.co/RlLh7SCRok.

If you want to sign up, you can use my ref link and you’ll earn a 10% bonus on any points you generate (and I will get a 10% bonus as well): https://t.co/hw0vyNvXcQ

100MW at Kearney is mining Bitcoin today and needs a lease and routine permits to convert. I estimate a deal on that first 100MW is worth about $1/share, even with Starwood taking 50%.

The additional 268MW depends on Nebraska Public Power District approving the new load. MARA has filed the application and posted the deposit, but I haven’t seen NPPD commit. If it does, the full 368MW is worth roughly $3.50/share (again assuming Starwood gets 50% of the economics). Until then I’d haircut that piece heavily.

Assumes $2M/MW rent on IT load and about $13M/MW to build. Note: these are my numbers, not MARA’s.

thread_tweets.text: אני לא רוצה להיכנס לשאלות מאוד בסיסיות. אני מציע שקודם תקדישי כמה ימים לחקור את הנושא, ואז אשמח לענות על כל השאלות. בעבר כבר פרסמתי כמה שווים היום הנכסים של צים לעומת השווי שבו נרשמו במקור. מדובר ברווחים אדירים של מיליארדי דולרים. בנוסף, אם תשקיעי כמה ימים בלימוד החברה, תגלי שצים צפויה לסיים את השנה עם מזומן של בין 29 ל־34 דולר למניה. הסכום המדויק תלוי בין היתר בתנודות במחירי הדלק. לגבי החוב, כמעט כולו נובע מחוזי חכירה של אוניות, שכיום שווי השוק שלהם גבוה משמעותית מהעלות החוזית שלהם. במילים פשוטות, אם אני חוכר אונייה במחיר X, והמחיר הנוכחי לחכירת אונייה דומה הוא X פלוס 5, הרי שלחוזה שלי יש ערך כלכלי חיובי. צים יכולה, אם תרצה ובכפוף לתנאי החוזים, להעביר את החכירות לצד שלישי ולממש רווחים אדירים. לכן, לפני ששואלים שאלות אחרי שתי דקות של הסתכלות על הנתונים, כדאי להשקיע כמה ימים בלימוד החברה, הדוחות והחוזים שלה. אחרי שתעשי שיעורי בית, אשמח לענות על כל שאלה.

In any conversation, there is a responsibility to express and a responsibility to listen.

Misinterpretations and misunderstandings are always going to happen. Often, difficulty in communication is due to people having different ways of thinking (e.g., left-brained thinkers talking to right-brained thinkers). 

The parties involved should always consider the possibility that one or both of them misunderstood and do a back-and-forth so that they can get in sync. #principleoftheday

But the stock market going up 1% after a bad headline?

THAT is apparently where we reach the limits of human imagination.

"For this run, each agent had a sandbox on its own lightweight virtual machine. A single shared machine hit its limits at about 100 agents: more than half of our 100-agent runs had to be stopped or restarted because memory, disk, or CPU ran out."

tweets.text:
quick observations from the claude fable and mythos 5.2 launch:

1/ it went from doing 21% of real freelance work to 41% in one release, so agencies are about to start charging per deliverable instead of per hour!

2/ it can work 10-12 hours on its own, which basically gives every small business a night shift (might as well use it if you know what you want to build)

3/ over 90% of anthropic's own code is now written by claude, and so i think the solo $1b founder is coming soon

4/ one engineer ran 1000+ subagents for 8 days and got an operating system that boots, so the ancient software running hospitals and airlines is finally rebuildable (lots of opportunity here on rebuilding)

5/ it designed 3 working electronic devices from a single prompt, which makes 1 person hardware companies a real thing

6/ it now says "i don't know" instead of guessing, and that's what law, medicine and finance have been waiting for (this has been the biggest thorn for these industries, hard to trust guessing)

7/ 1000 agents formalized fermat's last theorem in 30 hours, so software that's mathematically proven not to break is coming for payments and medical devices

8/ mythos is only for verified orgs, which means someone is going to build a business selling what only they have access to

9/ the models are getting better at noticing when they're being tested, so testing ai out in the real world is about to become its own industry

i love new model day
